Resampling Stability of the Item Assignment in a Confirmatory Model

Source: R/cfa_item_stability.R
cfa_item_stability.Rd

Checks, without leaving the confirmatory framework, whether each item of a CFA model would stay on its factor in another sample. The model is refitted on many subsamples and, one item at a time, the item is moved to each of the other factors. The item "lands" on the factor whose model fits best (lowest chi-square). The proportion of subsamples in which it lands on the factor the model assigns is its stability.

Unlike item_stability, which reruns efa_boosting() and therefore extracts factors on every resample, no exploratory step is involved: the factors are always those of the model, and only the place of one item changes at a time. This makes it suitable for checking a respecified CFA model, such as one in which some items were moved between factors, against the classic objection that the respecification capitalizes on chance (MacCallum, Roznowski & Necowitz, 1992).

Usage

cfa_item_stability(
  data,
  model,
  R = 200,
  prop = 0.8,
  threshold = 0.75,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  n_cores = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'cfa_item_stability'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

data

Data frame with the item responses. Columns not used by the model are ignored.

model

The model, either as a named list (factor name -> character vector of items) or as lavaan syntax with =~ lines only. At least two factors are required, and every item must load on one factor only.

R

Number of subsamples. Default 200.

prop

Proportion of cases drawn in each subsample, without replacement. Default 0.8.

threshold

Stability from which an item is read as stable. Default 0.75.

estimator

Estimator passed to lavaan::cfa(). Default "WLSMV".

ordered

Treat the items as ordinal. Default TRUE.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility; NULL (default) leaves the RNG untouched.

n_cores

Number of parallel workers. Default 1 (sequential). Values above 1 use a PSOCK cluster and require the package to be installed.

verbose

Print progress. Default TRUE.

x

A cfa_item_stability object.

digits

Number of digits for the printed values. Default 3.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class cfa_item_stability: a list with

items

one row per item: item, factor (the assigned factor), stability, other (the factor it lands on most often when it leaves its own), lambda_own (median standardized loading on its factor), lambda_moved (median loading when moved to its best alternative), delta_chisq (median chi-square of the best alternative minus that of the model: positive values favour the assigned factor), n_valid and reading.

fit

one row per subsample with the fit of the model as specified (cfi, tli, rmsea, srmr) and phi_max, the largest correlation between factors.

summary

success rate, median phi_max and the proportion of subsamples with phi_max below .90.

model, settings, call

the model as a named list, the settings used and the call.

Details

On each subsample the function fits:

  1. the model as specified, recording its fit and the largest correlation between factors; and

  2. for each item, one model per alternative factor, identical to the specified one except that the item loads on that factor instead of its own.

The item is moved, not duplicated, so every alternative has the same degrees of freedom as the specified model and their chi-squares (the unscaled test statistic, from the same subsample) compare directly. The item keeps its factor unless an alternative has a lower chi-square. Freeing a cross-loading instead would be fragile: with highly correlated factors it leaves the item's loadings nearly unidentified and yields inadmissible estimates. An alternative that would leave a factor with fewer than two items is not considered. Subsampling is without replacement, because duplicated cases distort the polychoric correlations that WLSMV relies on (see item_stability). The subsamples are drawn before any fitting, so results are reproducible with seed and identical for any n_cores.

Each item is read as "stable" when its stability is at least threshold, as "prefers other factor" when it is at most 1 - threshold, and as "unstable" in between.

References

MacCallum, R. C., Roznowski, M., & Necowitz, L. B. (1992). Model modifications in covariance structure analysis: The problem of capitalization on chance. Psychological Bulletin, 111(3), 490-504. doi:10.1037/0033-2909.111.3.490

See also

item_stability, algorithm_stability, cross_validate_cfa.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(Data_Expectativas)
model <- list(F1 = paste0("EAF", 1:5), F2 = paste0("EAF", 6:10))
st <- cfa_item_stability(Data_Expectativas, model, R = 5, seed = 1)
#> Fitting 5 subsamples sequentially...
